title: Off Campus
synopsis: Junior year. A hockey scholarship. A part-time job. A roommate situation that is, depending on the day, a romance. You have eighteen credits and one heart. Choose what to spend them on.

nodes.text: The off-campus house is bigger and dustier than the brochure suggested. Your three teammates haul a couch. Your maybe-girlfriend Hannah arrives, surprising everyone but you, with a houseplant.

choices.text: Help her find a spot for the plant
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Help her find a spot for the plant” back. Small choice shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Big choice.

nodes.text: Hannah and you wander the bookstore together. She buys a course pack. You buy a coffee. She holds your hand on the walk back like you've been together for a year. You haven't.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Define—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Don't talk about it; let it be
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Don't talk about it; let it be” back. Float shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Coach picks the captain on Friday. You are runner-up. Garrett, who deserves it, gets it. You realize you are equal parts relieved and disappointed, which is the most honest you've felt about hockey in a year.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Sportsmanship—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honesty—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Your part-time job at the campus bar starts. Tips are okay. The shift is until 2. Hockey practice is at 6 a.m. You realize you've signed up for, in the old phrase, the eighteen-hour day.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Triage.

choices.text: Push through; you can sleep in December
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Grit—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Hannah's parents visit campus for a weekend. They invite you to dinner. You realize you are now, suddenly, in 'meet the parents' territory. They are nice. Her dad asks you about hockey statistics.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Plain—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Be honest about your major” back. Pivot shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Three exams in a week. Your professor sees you fall asleep in lecture. He, kindly, does not call you out. He, kindly, also schedules you for office hours.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Go to office hours” back. Receive help shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
“Skip; sleep instead” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Body first.

nodes.text: A weekend tournament in Maine. You play well. Hannah cannot come. You text her between games. She is, you can tell, slightly bored of being texted between games.

choices.text: Call her after the late game
choices.consequence: Make the effort.
Trust the relationship.

nodes.text: Garrett, the captain, is in a slump. Coach is on him. He, off-ice, doesn't talk to anyone. You realize captain isn't, mostly, a prize. It is a weight.

choices.consequence: Be the teammate.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Respect.

nodes.text: Hannah's friend Maya tells you, gently and without saying so directly, that Hannah is tired of being the one who initiates. You realize this is true. You realize you are also, possibly, the one who is tired.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Repair.

choices.text: Have a real conversation about it
choices.consequence: You commit to “Have a real conversation about it.” The story records the instinct as “Address” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Coach calls you in. He wants to talk about whether you want hockey to be your life after graduation. He is honest about your ceiling. You realize you are honest with yourself for the first time about it too.

choices.text: Decide hockey is for college and beyond
choices.consequence: Bet on it.

choices.text: Decide hockey is for college, period
choices.consequence: Plan for after.

nodes.text: You sit on the porch with Hannah. The conversation is not perfect. The conversation is real. By the end you both know what the next month will be — and it is, surprisingly, more 'us' than you'd been managing.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Reset the relationship on purpose.” The story records the instinct as “Refresh” and carries it forward.
“Take it week by week” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Trial.

nodes.text: Three finals. Two late shifts at the bar. One playoff game. You sleep, total, twelve hours. You survive the week and your roommate hands you a beer at midnight on Friday. It is, briefly, the best beer of your life.

choices.consequence: “Go home for the break” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Family.
There is no taking “Stay in town with Hannah” back. Stay shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You go to the career fair in a borrowed blazer. You hand out résumés. You realize the future is, against expectations, available. You also realize most of the recruiters at this fair are looking at hockey players for, of all things, sales.

choices.text: Talk to a tech company that interests you
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Talk to a tech company that interests you” back. Aim shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Talk to the kind sales recruiter
choices.consequence: There is no taking “Talk to the kind sales recruiter” back. Pragmatic shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Spring is gentler. You drop a class. You take a writing class instead. The writing class is, embarrassingly, the best class you have taken in college.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discover.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Pragmatic—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: End of the year. Captains for next season are voted on. Your name is on the list. So is Garrett's, again. You realize you might, this time, want it.

choices.consequence: “Accept the nomination” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Lead.
There is no taking “Decline and support Garrett” back. Servant leader shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Senior year arrives. You are captain or you aren't. You and Hannah are still, somehow, together. Your professor invites you to TA the intro writing course. The houseplant is huge.

choices.consequence: Build the after.

choices.text: Focus only on hockey and Hannah
choices.consequence: Live the season.

nodes.text: Cap and gown. Your family in the bleachers. Hannah ahead of you in line. Garrett behind you. Coach watching from the side. You realize, for one second, that this is the moment you'll think about when life is hard later.

choices.text: Take a mental photo to keep forever
choices.consequence: “Take a mental photo to keep forever” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Save it.

choices.text: Plan a road trip with Hannah for the summer
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Forward—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Senior night. The rink lights, the parents standing, your name read over the PA. You realize this might be the last time you skate in front of people who came because of you.

choices.consequence: “Take it in fully” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Be present.

choices.text: Play it like every other game
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Discipline—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: After graduation Hannah and you walk through a small apartment near the city. The kitchen tiles are ugly. The window has good light. You decide together what the year after college looks like.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Commit.

choices.text: Wait six months and travel first
choices.consequence: You commit to “Wait six months and travel first.” The story records the instinct as “Open” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: First real Monday after college. The world is, finally, not a syllabus. You sit on a porch and look at it. You decide which version of your life starts now.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Build the after.” The story records the instinct as “Career on” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Stay present for now” back. Lean in shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Drive west.

nodes.text: You finish college with options. You take a job that lets you write. Hockey becomes a Saturday morning thing. Hannah, who matured into being your favorite person, ends up at the same magazine for a year. You build the after on purpose.

Years later, on a long Saturday, you'll remember this day clearly — the bleachers, the lake, the friends. You'll be sitting on a porch with kids running around. You'll feel, briefly, the way you felt at twenty-one. You'll be grateful.

Hannah and you drive across the country in a beat-up car. You stop in towns you can't pronounce. You eat at diners. You take a photo at every state border. The photos live in a shoebox you never quite organize. You don't need to.
